The '''1994–95 Primeira Divisão''' was the [[Primeira Liga#All-time Primeira Liga table|61st edition]] of top flight of Portuguese football. It started on 21 August 1994 with a match between [[C.F. Os Belenenses|Belenenses]] and [[C.F. Estrela da Amadora|Estrela da Amadora]], and ended on 28 May 1995. The league was contested by 18 clubs with [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] as the defending champions.

Porto won the league and qualified for the [[1995–96 UEFA Champions League]] group stage, Sporting qualified for the [[1994–95 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]] first round, and [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], [[Vitória S.C.|Vitória de Guimarães]] and [[S.C. Farense|Farense]] qualified for the [[1995–96 UEFA Cup]]; in opposite, [[C.F. União|União da Madeira]], [[S.C. Beira-Mar|Beira-Mar]] and [[Vitória F.C.|Vitória de Setúbal]] were relegated to the [[Liga de Honra]]. [[Hassan Nader|Hassan]]  was the top scorer with 21 goals.

This was the final season in which two points were awarded for a win; going forward this changed to [[Three points for a win|three points]].

==Promotion and relegation==

===Teams relegated to [[Liga de Honra]]===
*[[F.C. Paços de Ferreira|Paços de Ferreira]]
*[[F.C. Famalicão|Famalicão]]
*[[G.D. Estoril-Praia|Estoril-Praia]]

Paços de Ferreira, Famalicão and Estoril-Praia, were consigned to the Liga de Honra following their final classification in [[1993–94 Primeira Divisão|1993–94 season]].

===Teams promoted from Liga de Honra===
*[[F.C. Tirsense|Tirsense]]
*[[U.D. Leiria|União de Leiria]]
*[[G.D. Chaves|Chaves]]

The other three teams were replaced by Tirsense, União de Leiria and Chaves from the Liga de Honra.
